result.topic_en: A letter from G. H. Hardy to G. N. Watson reporting that Miss Stanley has brought him a large bundle of Ramanujan manuscripts, and describing one rough set of notes about a Mellin-type integral formula and Fourier integrals.
result.transcription:
Postmark 1930
Add ms a 94 18(1)

Dear Watson
Miss Stanley, who is staying here this week
end, and came to see me recently,
brought me a large bundle of Ramanujan
MSS, mostly fragmentary, but clear and
neat.
Some of the notes are old ones, and
refer to things mainly in the Papers or
in his note books: but not all. There
is one set, rougher than most, about
the formula
$\int w^{s-1}(a_0 - a_1 w + \cdots)\,dw = \frac{\pi}{\sin \pi s}\,a_{-s}$
(a sort of alias of Mellin: see my
'Carlson-Wigert' paper in Acta 42),
Fourier's $\int\int$, etc, etc — all mixed up in
a fine old stew. This I gave back to her,
after a lecture, because I thought it might
suggest something for her to work at. There
are some other things I mean to talk to
her about tomorrow. But there is a
substantial chunk which I think I sh[?]

methods.what: Ramanujan's master theorem / Mellin-transform formula: the integral of w^{s-1} times an alternating power series equals pi/sin(pi s) times the coefficient a_{-s}
Fourier's double integral (Fourier integral theorem), mentioned only by name
